title: TRON configuration: routing.yaml
description: This TRON execution instance's own scope/eligibility configuration (PID §4.3: one execution instance per broker/account context). This is deliberately NOT an upstream-destination routing field on any canonical message — falcon.trade_action.v1 and tron.trade_intent.v1 have no such field by design (see 05-CONTRACTS.md §4/§5). This file exists per DEC-OPEN-06's PROPOSED (not decided) policy: 'actions remain broker-neutral; TRON instance configuration determines its eligible actions.' If Product Authority resolves DEC-OPEN-06 differently (e.g. a per-message routing/destination field), this schema's instance-scope fields remain valid alongside it — an execution instance still needs to know its own broker/account context and eligibility regardless of how per-message routing is eventually decided; nothing here forecloses that future answer. Contract-owner of this file: WI-D (WO-TRON-D1).

identifier.description: Stable opaque identifier. Never a real account login, credential, or other sensitive infrastructure identifier (HR-10) — this is a symbolic label only, resolved to real broker/account context by a separate, non-repository secrets mechanism.

instrument_name.description: Instrument identifier string, consistent with mapping.schema.json's canonical_instrument keys.

config_schema_version.description: Configuration schema major version for this file. Must equal "1". See 07-CONFIGURATION.md §2.

instance_id.description: Stable label identifying this TRON execution instance. Used for operational identification and event correlation, never as a broker account identifier itself.

broker_context.description: Symbolic label identifying which single configured broker/account context this instance serves (PID §4.3). This is a reference to a separately-managed, non-repository credential/context binding, never a literal account number, login, or other sensitive identifier (HR-10).

eligible_instruments.description: Canonical instruments this instance is eligible to act on. Absent means: all canonical instruments present in mapping.falcon.yaml's mapping table are eligible for this instance. An empty array explicitly means: no instrument is currently eligible (this instance accepts no OPEN actions), distinct from 'absent'.

eligible_actions.description: falcon.trade_action.v1 'action' values this instance is eligible to process. Absent means: all action values defined by falcon.trade_action.v1 (OPEN, CLOSE, MODIFY, CANCEL) are eligible for this instance.
